what: Blind A/B votes from a human reviewer, the only ground truth the LLM judge and the fixtures can be checked against. Collected through .lavish/grouping-verdicts.html: two layouts of one diff, sides shuffled per diff, nothing saying which came from the model.
summary: Six votes, six for the model's grouping over the hand-written fixture. The opus-5 judge decided two of those six the other way and left the rest undecided, so on the only evidence there is, the judge does not track the reviewer — and neither do the fixtures it is scored against.

rounds.replies: recorded before `trailTests`, so each source file still sat with its own test

votes.note: A is more descriptive, what happens in the files. But I still would like the tests in their own section at the bottom I think.
Same argument as the previous one. Would be perfect if all tests formed the last group, which I can then just ignore.

rounds.replies: recorded after `trailTests`, so every layout already ends in one group of tests

what_it_means: The reviewer prefers the model's finer, more descriptive groups to the fixtures' three or four broad ones — which is exactly what the fixtures, and therefore ARI, penalise.
The judge reasons about the same rules the prompt states and still lands on the fixture, so it is closer to the fixture author's taste than to the reviewer's.
Next: rewrite the fixtures around what the reviewer actually chose, or score against these votes directly. Until then, read both automatic numbers as regression detectors, not as verdicts.
